_comment: Hand-curated roster. scripts/resolve.py turns this into manifests/lock.json + the .mrpack index. Required dependencies are pulled in automatically. 'allow' widens the accepted release channel; 'pin' forces an exact Modrinth version id.

renderer.why: Renderer foundation required by Roxy/Voxy and Iris.
Translation layer that runs the original Voxy jar on NeoForge 1.21.1.
Long-distance LOD renderer. Roxy's only verified jar: voxy-0.2.16-beta for MC 1.21.11 (loaded through Roxy, not natively).
Generates real chunks in the background and feeds them to Voxy, so distant LODs match the modded terrain exactly (no seed approximation). Roxy ships compat for this v2 line.
Fabric API surface required by Roxy/Voxy.
Extra Sodium toggles used by the Performance profile (particles, animations, fog).
Usable video settings UI for Sodium's expanded option set.

performance.why: Load time and memory reduction; biggest single win for large packs.
Server-tick optimisations (AI, collisions, chunk ticking). NeoForge build.
Skips rendering hidden entities/block entities - important with large factories.
Lower FPS when the window is unfocused.
Raises packet size limits for large modpacks.
Leaves decay quickly after trees are cut.

worldgen.why: Biome foundation: ~95 vanilla-block biomes, cave biomes, works with vanilla tooling and Voxy's server-side LOD build.
Terrain shaping: huge mountain ranges, deep valleys, rivers; officially Terralith-compatible.
Nether biome + structure overhaul (Stardust Labs). Only 1.21.1 build is tagged alpha upstream; smoke-tested.
End terrain overhaul (Stardust Labs) - gives the End exploration value.
Extra biomes (re-added by the owner in 0.5; stacks with Terralith - check biome placement on a new world).
Cave biomes (re-added by the owner in 0.5; overlaps Terralith's cave biomes).
Biome API required by YUNG's Cave Biomes and Regions Unexplored (their mods.toml requires it; Modrinth metadata does not list it, so the resolver never pulled it in). Pinned to the 0.5 instance jar.

structures.why: Rare/legendary tier: huge hand-built dungeons and landmarks.
Biome-matched variants of vanilla structures; very configurable rarity.
Settlements and pillager outposts with regional variety.
Common/uncommon tier: small vanilla-styled ruins, camps and shrines.
Uncommon tier: taverns, illager hideouts, ancient ruins.
Common tier: atmospheric ruins and minor discoveries.
Integrated Dungeons and Structures: hand-built dungeons and towers.
Villages placed on flatter, sensible ground.
Small ruins with loot across biomes.
Spreads structure spacing so the larger structure set does not crowd.

dimensions.why: Sky dimension with three dungeon bosses and its own gear line.
Otherside dimension beyond Ancient Cities; Warden-tier progression.
Unique bee dimension with its own challenge/quest-like progression.
Underground dimension with a boss and its own material tier.
Rockets and planets: late-game space exploration.

rpg.why: Core loot system: affixes, rarities, gems, sockets, world tiers, bosses.
Attribute framework used by Apotheosis (crit, armor pierce, etc.).
Enchanting overhaul; gives enchanting long-term depth.
Weapon variety with unique uniques; Better Combat movesets built in.

Accessory slot framework. Pinned to 9.5.1: Curios 9.6.0 reworked CuriosEntityManager and the Accessories compat layer 0.1.13 mixin into it fails (crash on world load). Unpin once a newer compat layer supports 9.6.
Levelling relics found in structures (rare/legendary loot).
Late-game structure bosses with progression-defining drops.
Mid-game overworld mini-bosses that make exploring dangerous.
Provides mod id 'octolib' required by Relics 0.10.x (undeclared in Modrinth metadata; found by launch test).

Bounded, readable wave challenges (fixed waves, fixed entity counts, visible timer). Activates the gateway data Apotheosis already ships and hosts Horizon's late-game Trials, which consume exploration relics instead of producing them.
Accessory slot framework (Wisp Forest); Curios mods are routed into it by the compat layer, one accessory UI for the whole pack.
Routes the Curios API (Artifacts, Relics, Dream Relics) into Accessories so every accessory shares one set of slots.
Elytra and Totem of Undying can be worn in Accessories slots.
Spyglass, lantern, clock, compass and other vanilla tools work from an accessory slot.
Extra unique accessories. Not yet in the loot budget (docs/LOOT_BUDGET.md).
Terraria-style accessories. Not yet in the loot budget (docs/LOOT_BUDGET.md).

magic.why: Combat magic: schools, spellbooks, scroll loot, boss encounters.
Utility/automation magic: glyph spells, mana, rituals, item transport.
Spirit-based automation and storage; ritual crafting.
Iron's Spells requires irons_lib >=1.21.1-2 <1.21.1-3 (undeclared in Modrinth metadata; found by launch test).

technology.why: Bridges Create rotational power and FE electricity.
Liquid XP + automated enchanting; ties Create to Apotheosis enchanting.
Deep multiblock industrial progression (steam -> electric -> fusion).
Mid-game FE generation tiers, simple to learn.
Digital storage and autocrafting across all tech mods.
MEGA Cells: late-game AE2 storage tiers.
Ore multiplication, chemistry, jetpacks/MekaSuit - the mid-game processing pillar.
Mekanism power line up to fission/fusion.
Official AE2 storage/autocrafting of Mekanism chemicals.
Programmable computers/turtles; CC tags its stable line as beta.

qol.why: Primary recipe viewer with recipe trees.
Loads JEI-only plugins (Create, etc.); EMI hides JEI's UI.
Discoverable fast travel - must be found in villages/structures.
Resolves recipe output conflicts between mods.
Food variety that makes survival more than bread.
Quest book (Heracles). FTB Quests is CurseForge-only and cannot be in an .mrpack.

Per-player structure loot: each player opens their own copy of every structure container, so the expedition reward budget (docs/LOOT.md) holds per player in multiplayer instead of first-come-first-served.
Death recovery: items stay in a corpse at the death spot (also for void deaths) instead of despawning, so dying costs a trip back, not the whole kit.
Smooth client-side zoom for scouting distant terrain and structures.
In-game browser/updater for resource packs, data packs and shaders.
Extra inventory mouse shortcuts on top of Mouse Tweaks.
Stops Mouse Tweaks' wheel tweak misbehaving in the Accessories screen.
Sinytra Connector: loads Fabric mods on NeoForge.

atmosphere.why: Configurable ambient polish (fireflies, sparks, steam, dust, biome particles). Weather particles stay with Particle Rain; overlapping options are disabled in config.

fx.why: Visuality: hit/crystal/water-splash particles. Ambient-particle overlap with Subtle Effects resolved in config.
Better Clouds: Sodium/Iris-aware cloud renderer. Profile-controlled.
Cozy Critters & Creepy Crawlies: client-side ambient critters. Profile-controlled density.
Interactive Foliage: plants bend around entities (needs Sway).
Fancy World Animations: block open/close animations. Lantern swing owned by Swinging Lanterns.
Visual Overhaul: model polish for vanilla blocks/items.
Inventory Particles: particles on item interactions in GUIs.
Footprint Particle: footprints on soft blocks. Profile-controlled.
Cave Dust: underground dust particles; owns cave dust (Subtle Effects equivalent off).
Effectual: ambient particles; overlapping Subtle Effects categories disabled.
Clear Despawn: items blink before despawning.

audio.why: Sound Controller: per-sound volume control for overlapping sound mods.

camera_anim.why: Punchy Moves: first-person attack animations (beta). Fluid & Foolish (its required animation pack) is installed as a resource pack.
Auto Third Person: camera while riding/swimming/gliding.
Seamless Sleep: smooth time passage while sleeping.

ui.why: Last World Panorama: title panorama from the last world.

world_ext.why: Streams Reflowing: flowing streams worldgen. New chunks only.
Moog's Mineshafts Reimagined (overlaps YUNG's Better Mineshafts; see COMPATIBILITY.md).
TW's Decorative Food: placeable food decor.

content_ext.why: Bosses of Mass Destruction (existing NeoForge port).
Clavis: key-and-lock dungeon loot. DISABLED BY DEFAULT (0.3.1): lockpicking cursor bug not verified fixed; see docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md. Enable by renaming mods/*.jar.disabled to .jar.
Gear upgrade materials found in the world.
Library for the Integrated structure mods.

animation.why: EMF: required for Fresh Animations (no OptiFine).
ETF: required for Fresh Animations and emissives.

cosmetics.why: Simple Hats: wearable hats (head slot). 0.3.1: a few rare hats are quest and dungeon rewards (horizon loot + KubeJS), the rest unlocked by the mod's own system.

shaders.why: Default shader. Voxy support since r5.8.1. r5.9.3 chosen over r5.10 (3 days old).

rejected.the-twilight-forest: CurseForge-only; not distributable through Modrinth .mrpack. Documented as optional manual add-on.
rejected.c2me-neoforge: Alpha; worldgen threading risk with heavy worldgen datapacks.
rejected.noisium: Last 1.21.1 build Aug 2024; overlaps with Lithostitched/Tectonic noise handling.
rejected.enderio: 1.21.1 line is beta-only; MI + Powah + Create Additions cover its role.
rejected.industrial-foregoing: Requires Titanium beta; overlaps MI. Excluded for stability.
rejected.simplymore: Only an alpha build (1.3.0_alpha5) for NeoForge 1.21.1; would dilute the Simply Swords/Apotheosis weapon pool.
rejected.particular-reforged: Overlaps Subtle Effects (ambient particles). One ambient-particle mod is enough; Subtle Effects has finer per-effect config.
rejected.loot-beams-refork: Apotheosis already draws rarity beams/particles for affix items; a second beam renderer duplicates them. Horizon finds use server-side pickup feedback instead.
rejected.explorers-compass / natures-compass: Point-to-anything compasses remove discovery. Clues come from exploration maps in loot and quest guidance instead.
rejected.biomes-o-plenty / oh-the-biomes-weve-gon: Would stack another biome-placement system on top of Terralith + Regions Unexplored.
rejected.sodium-dynamic-lights / sodium-options-a: 0.5: Sodium Options API (last build 2025-01) requires Reese's Sodium Options, and every Reese's for Sodium 0.8 declares Options API incompatible, so neither loads. Sodium Dynamic Lights needs Options API; Immersive Lanterns 1.0.6 hard-requires Sodium Dynamic Lights.

resourcepacks.why: FA Details 2.4.0 (0.3.1): extra detail on vanilla mobs. Replaces the All-Extensions bundle so Objects, Spiders, Creepers, Classic Horses and Player stay off until each is checked.
FA Emissive 1.7.0 (0.3.1): glowing eyes/parts via ETF emissive support.
FA Quivers 2.3.0 (0.3.1): quivers on skeletons/players' backs; no conflict with Better Combat or Simply Swords.
Required animation pack for Punchy Moves (separate from FA mob stack).

excluded.reason: Its always-on built-in datapack (infinity_cave_terralith when Terralith is loaded) replaces minecraft:dimension/overworld, minecraft:dimension_type/overworld (min_y -128, height 448), minecraft:worldgen/noise_settings/overworld and every vanilla biome file. Terralith also overrides dimension/overworld and Tectonic overrides noise_settings/overworld, so one terrain system silently loses. The dimension_type change also applies to existing 0.2.0 saves (overworld height changes under already-generated chunks). Needs a merged Tectonic+Terralith+Infinity Cave noise router and a new-world-only rollout; not attempted in this pass.
F.M.R.P 3.0.5 only ships EMF models for friendsandfoes, frostiful, guardvillagers, savage_and_ravage and takesapillage; none is in Horizon, so it would animate nothing.
Targets Supplementaries, Quark, Sleep Tight and You've Goat to be Kidding Me; none is in Horizon.
Patches for illager mods that are not in Horizon.

excluded.status: not installed (FA addon, conflicts with requested Punchy Moves)
excluded.reason: In game (0.3.0 candidate) Punchy Moves shows a Conflicting Animations screen: "Punchy Moves is not compatible with Fresh Animations: Player Extension". Punchy Moves is a requested entry; the player extension is optional, so player animation is owned by Punchy/Punchy Moves (+ Better Combat for its weapons).
Declares FA Player Extension as required; removed with it.

1.1.6 exists only as a datapack / Fabric-Forge jar. Its data overrides minecraft:dimension/overworld (Terralith's biome source), minecraft:worldgen/noise_settings/overworld (Tectonic's) and 37 vanilla biomes, so installing it replaces Terralith or Tectonic terrain; its Tectonic compat exists only for 1.21.5+. Needs a merged biome source/noise router; new worlds only.

Resource pack exists only for 1.21.9+ (item-definition files + 1.21.9 overlays/core shaders). The item switching could be expressed with neoforge:separate_transforms, but the 3D models use free element rotation angles (12.5, 15, 25 deg..., 360+ elements) that the 1.21.1 model loader rejects; adapting means snapping angles (visible distortion) or a model-loader patch.

Native NeoForge 1.21.1 build exists on CurseForge only, licensed All Rights Reserved: it cannot be embedded in the .mrpack and Modrinth packs cannot reference CurseForge downloads. Manual install possible per docs/EXPANSION_CHECKLIST.md; not tested in this pass.
CurseForge-only, All Rights Reserved, no NeoForge 1.21.1 build and no public source: a port needs the author's permission and source.
Source is public but All Rights Reserved; NeoForge builds exist only for 1.21.5+. A back-port would need the author's permission.
Fabric only, All Rights Reserved; porting needs the author's permission.
All Rights Reserved, no source, no NeoForge 1.21.1 build.

GPL-3.0 source available (1.21.4+ Fabric, Mojang-mapped). Port is permitted but invasive: it replaces the vanilla minecraft:sand/red_sand/suspicious_sand registrations through a Registry.register mixin, uses 1.21.2+ Properties.setId, and its mod id wet-sand is invalid on NeoForge. Deferred, not attempted in this pass.
CC0 source (Da0neDatGotAway/better-enchants) currently targets 26.2 (~2.9k lines of render code); the 1.21.4-era revision has not been ported in this pass.
LGPL-3.0 source exists only for Forge 1.20.1 (~1.1k lines); a NeoForge 1.21.1 port was not attempted in this pass.
0.3.1: split out of the All-Extensions bundle; not enabled until checked in game.

0.3.1: held back. Spider Overhaul adds 14 spider entity types with their own models; FA Spiders would re-animate only vanilla spiders, so the two would look different side by side. Not checked visually.

0.3.1: split out of the All-Extensions bundle so each add-on is chosen on purpose. Objects animates chests, doors and other blocks via EMF; not enabled until checked in game against Sophisticated Storage, Lootr and Create block models (their blocks are modded, so Objects only touches vanilla blocks).
0.3.1: split out of the All-Extensions bundle; not enabled until checked in game.

0.3.1: the All-Extensions bundle was replaced by the individual Details, Emissive and Quivers packs (pinned in the roster); Objects, Spiders, Creepers and Classic Horses are held back, Player stays dropped (Punchy Moves conflict).

instance_only._comment: In the ProjectHorizon-0.5 instance but not on Modrinth, so not in the .mrpack. Add by hand, or port/embed if the licence allows.
instance_only.NeoForge-terrain-diffusion-mc-2.3.0-wind: Terrain Diffusion. Windows-only build: would break Linux/macOS clients and servers if shipped.
Regions Unexplored x Terrain Diffusion bridge.
instance_only.dtarsnouveau-1.3.0.jar: Dynamic Trees for Ars Nouveau trees.
instance_only.mobdismembermentneoforge-1.21.1-1.4.0.ja: Hand-added before 0.5 (the roster's excluded list notes no NeoForge port existed).
